ideas.description: On the E046 tip (bs 1536, 3@16 + 1@24 + 4@32 px, compiled Muon on 9 convs plus head), set torch._dynamo.config.automatic_dynamic_shapes=False and raise torch._dynamo.config.cache_size_limit (e.g. 64) so that each (resolution, batch) train shape (16/24/32 px at bs 1536, plus any partial last-batch shapes) compiles as its own static graph. Warm all of them up in build on synthetic data. Keep eval on a separate compiled function that is dynamic in the batch dimension (torch._dynamo.mark_dynamic on dim 0, or the existing eval path unchanged), so any B from 1 to 1024 never recompiles. In an untimed side check, verify eval for B in {1, 7, 1000, 1024} returns finite [B,100] logits in under 5 s with no recompile. Change no math, hyperparameters or schedule. Log per-phase epoch times.
ideas.expected: Time ~4.87-4.89 s (-1.3 to -1.7% vs 4.955 s; E045's micro-benchmark measured ~0.086 s/trial, mostly in the 24 and 32 px phases). Accuracy unchanged within noise (~0.753-0.756). If it is >=0.7535 with time <=4.89 s, bank it as the new tip; a math-identical change only needs the time improvement plus accuracy inside the noise band. If time drops by <0.5%, the micro-benchmark gain does not survive the full run and H2.14.1 is refuted.

ideas.description: On the static-shape tip (or on E046 if H2.14.1 fails), trim a quarter of the remaining 24 px bridge with a step-indexed switch: 3@16 + 0.75@24 + 4@32 px (7.75 epochs). Rescale the LR warmup/decay, EMA, lookahead and renorm schedules to the new total step count, exactly as E047 did. Change nothing else, and use only shapes already warmed up in build. This trim is half the size of H2.10.2's arm A on purpose: at ~0.03 pp per 1%, the ~0.15 pp margin only covers a ~2-3% trim, while arm A (-0.26 s) would be expected to land at ~0.7532, right on the gate.
ideas.expected: Time -0.12 to -0.14 s (~-2.5%, about 4.75 s if the static-shape tip is banked, or ~4.83 s on E046). Accuracy -0.05 to -0.12 pp, two-run mean ~0.7537-0.7545. New tip only under the H4 rule (3-seed mean >=0.755, or two non-bit-identical runs averaging >=0.7535). A loss of >=0.2 pp means the third 16 px swap already made the 24 px bridge binding, and H2.10's fractional-trim line on the bridge is closed.

ideas.description: On the static-shape tip (or on E046 if that fails), replace AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) with x.flatten(2).amax(dim=2), which is mathematically identical (Fable: it avoids slow atomic kernels). Recompile and warm up every train and eval shape in build. Change nothing else.
ideas.expected: Time -0.3 to -1% (roughly -0.015 to -0.05 s), with most of the gain in the backward pass of the 16 px phase (1x1 final map) and the 24 px phase (2x2 final map). Accuracy within noise (>=0.7535). Bank it if time drops >=0.5% with accuracy in the noise band. A drop under 0.3% is time noise, which closes the pool lever.

ideas.description: On the E046 tip (or on the static-shape tip if it is banked first), lower the LR floor of the Muon groups only (9 conv filter groups plus the head) from 0.07x to 0.05x of peak. Keep the SGD groups' floor, the warmup, the peak LR and the EMA/lookahead unchanged. Pass the value as the existing 0-d tensor schedule so nothing recompiles.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Accuracy -0.15 to +0.25 pp vs the 0.7548 two-run mean. If the 3-seed mean is >=0.7563, rerun to confirm (H4 rule); a confirmed gain buys margin for one further fractional trim. A result within ±0.15 pp closes the Muon floor, and with it LR-schedule tuning for Muon.

ideas.description: On the E046 tip, double the LR warmup length (0.23 -> 0.46 of the warmup fraction in steps) for both the SGD and Muon groups, keeping the same peak and the same decay end point. Change nothing else. This is the untested direction after E051, where halving the warmup cost ~0.2 pp.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Accuracy -0.2 to +0.3 pp vs 0.7548. A 3-seed mean >=0.7563 supports H6.4/H8 (early training is step-starved or LR-fragile) and becomes a margin source, pending a confirming rerun. A result within ±0.15 pp closes warmup length in both directions. A loss of >=0.2 pp means the current warmup sits at a sharp optimum.

ideas.description: On the E046 tip, halve the warmup only for the Muon groups (conv filters plus head). The SGD groups (BN biases at 64x LR, whitening bias, head bias) keep the current warmup. Same peak and decay end point, no recompiles (separate 0-d LR tensors per group already exist).
ideas.expected: Time unchanged. Accuracy 0.7530-0.7555, i.e. no loss beyond noise vs 0.7548, unlike E051's -0.2 pp from halving both. That would support the claim that the warmup protects the SGD bias groups, and it would point at bias-LR levers (next idea) as the early-phase margin source. If the result is <=0.7525, Muon itself needs the warmup, and the H8.1 bias channel is refuted.

ideas.description: On the E046 tip, train the whitening-stem bias only for the first 20% of steps and freeze it after that (as in hiverge and Fable). Set its LR to 0 from step 0.2*total, either through its own 0-d LR tensor or by masking it in the SGD foreach step, so nothing recompiles. Everything else is unchanged. This tests whether the 64x-LR bias groups add late-phase noise in the ~256-step regime.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged or -0.1% (a few fewer elementwise ops). Accuracy -0.1 to +0.25 pp vs 0.7548. A 3-seed mean >=0.7563 (then confirmed by a rerun) gives a zero-cost margin source to spend on a fractional trim. A result within ±0.15 pp closes it.

structured_output.summary:
The tip is E046 at 4.955 s, with a two-run mean of 0.7548 and ~0.15 pp of local margin. The new ideas fall into three groups.

**Time levers (exploit):**
- Static per-resolution compile graphs (H2.14.1), priority 5. This is the cheapest zero-accuracy lever, measured at about -1.6% in E045's micro-benchmark.
- Swapping AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) for flatten+amax (H2.14.2).
- A deliberately small fractional trim of the 24 px bridge (H2.10), 3@16 + 0.75@24 + 4@32. It is sized to fit the ~0.15 pp margin at ~0.03 pp per 1% of time. H2.10.2's full arm A, at -0.26 s, would land right on the 0.753 gate.

**Zero-cost accuracy probes (explore):**
- A lower Muon LR floor (H6.5.1).
- Doubled warmup (H6.4.2).
- Halving the warmup for the Muon groups only (H8.1.2), to locate the mechanism behind E051's -0.2 pp.
- Freezing the whitening bias after 20% of steps (H8.1, the hiverge/Fable practice).

**Queue:** nothing is dropped. I061 (prepare overhead on the 5 s run) is still a valid, cheap test. I060 (per-phase profiling, still running) gates the CUDA-graph and Muon-overlap ideas (H2.12.1/H2.12.2), so I left those unqueued. The Muon lr 0.28 re-check (H7.1.3), the head step-size diagnostic (H7.3.1), the per-layer width profile (H2.13.2) and the bs-768 first half-epoch (H8.1.1) wait until these runs report. Any result that would become a new tip still needs the H4 confirming rerun.
